objectives: Map the microbiome revolution + clinical applications.
Frame AI + synthetic biology for microbiology.

slides.title: The microbiome — gut, skin, oral + the second genome
slides.body:
**Human microbiome** = the trillions of microbial cells (bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses, protists) inhabiting our body surfaces. ~10¹³-10¹⁴ microbial cells per person, comparable to host cells (older 10:1 estimate revised down by Sender, Fuchs + Milo 2016 to ~1:1). Microbial genes outnumber human genes ~100:1 — the **'second genome.'**

**Body-site communities** — distinct anatomical biogeographies:

- **Gut (colon)** — most numerous + studied; dominated by **Bacteroidetes** (Bacteroides, Prevotella) + **Firmicutes** (Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Faecalibacterium, Roseburia) + smaller Actinobacteria (Bifidobacterium), Proteobacteria, Verrucomicrobia (Akkermansia muciniphila), archaea (Methanobrevibacter smithii). >1000 species per individual; ~150-200 'core' species shared widely; enormous strain-level variation.
- **Skin** — *Cutibacterium* (formerly Propionibacterium) on sebaceous; *Staphylococcus* (epidermidis, hominis) on moist; *Corynebacterium*; fungi (*Malassezia*); body-site- + individual-specific.
- **Oral** — >700 species; *Streptococcus*, *Veillonella*, *Neisseria*, *Prevotella*, *Fusobacterium*. Distinct subhabitats: tongue dorsum, saliva, supragingival + subgingival plaque, buccal mucosa. Disrupted in periodontitis (red complex: *Porphyromonas gingivalis*, *Treponema denticola*, *Tannerella forsythia*).
- **Vaginal** — *Lactobacillus* dominance (L. crispatus, L. iners, L. gasseri, L. jensenii) in most reproductive-age women; produces lactic acid → low pH → protective. Disruption → bacterial vaginosis (BV; Gardnerella, Atopobium, Megasphaera).
- **Respiratory** — sparse but present; upper airway commensals (*Moraxella*, *Streptococcus*); lung microbiome real + relevant (was once thought sterile).
- **Urinary** — also no longer considered sterile; sparse but defined community.

**Major projects + figures**:
- **Human Microbiome Project (HMP)** Phase 1 (NIH, 2007-2014, ~$170M): characterized microbiomes of ~300 healthy adults at 18 body sites using 16S rRNA + shotgun metagenomics. Phase 2 (iHMP, 2014-2018) integrated metagenomics + metabolomics + host data in disease cohorts (IBD, type 2 diabetes pregnancy).
- **MetaHIT** (European, gut focus, 2008-2012).
- **Earth Microbiome Project** (Knight + Gilbert 2010-): global standardized characterization of microbiomes across all of Earth (~30000 samples now).
- ***Rob Knight*** (UCSD) — co-founder of EMP + American Gut + Qiita + QIIME software (the standard 16S/metagenomic analysis pipeline; QIIME 2 now). Reframed how we sample + analyze microbiomes at scale.
- ***Jeffrey Gordon*** (Washington University, St Louis) — pioneer of germ-free mice + microbiome-host biology. Showed that obesity is transmissible via microbiome transplant from obese-mouse → germ-free mouse (Turnbaugh, Ridaura + Gordon 2006-2013); foundational malnutrition-microbiome work in Malawi + Bangladesh childhood-stunting cohorts.

**Microbiome + disease — selected links** (correlation strong; causation often emerging):

- **Obesity + metabolism**: increased Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio + altered SCFA production; transmissible via fecal transplant in mice (Turnbaugh-Gordon 2006). Bariatric surgery shifts microbiome dramatically; some metabolic-surgery benefit may be microbiome-mediated.
- **Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD)**: dysbiosis with decreased *Faecalibacterium prausnitzii* (anti-inflammatory butyrate producer), increased adherent-invasive *E. coli*. Major Crohn's + UC association.
- **IBS (Irritable Bowel Syndrome)**: dysbiosis + altered bile-acid metabolism + low-grade inflammation; rifaximin (non-absorbed antibiotic) + probiotics modest benefit.
- **C. difficile colitis** — post-antibiotic dysbiosis → C. diff overgrowth → AAD → pseudomembranous colitis → recurrent C. diff. **Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT)** ~85-90% cure rate for recurrent C. diff (van Nood 2013 NEJM); now FDA-approved products (**Rebyota** 2022, **Vowst** 2023 oral). One of the great clinical-microbiology success stories.
- **Allergy + asthma**: 'hygiene hypothesis' / 'old friends' (Strachan, Rook); reduced early-life microbial exposure → Th2-skewed immunity → atopy. Birth mode (vaginal vs C-section), breastfeeding, antibiotic exposure modulate.
- **Autism + behavior**: gut-brain axis; preliminary microbiome differences + animal-model causal links (Hsiao); microbiome-based interventions in trials.
- **Cancer immunotherapy response**: gut microbiome composition predicts response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 (Gopalakrishnan + Zitvogel 2018); FMT + microbiome modulation now in immuno-oncology trials.
- **Cardiovascular**: TMAO from microbial choline + carnitine metabolism → atherosclerosis (Hazen).
- **Neurodegeneration**: Parkinson + Alzheimer microbiome associations under intense study; gut-brain vagal + immune + metabolite axes.
- **Mental health**: depression, anxiety links via gut-brain axis; emerging.

**Germ-free vs SPF mice** — foundational tools (developed at Notre Dame + Lobund + Karolinska):
- **Germ-free (axenic, gnotobiotic) mice** — born + raised in sterile isolators; no microbiome. Underdeveloped gut, immature immune system, altered metabolism. Used to study microbiome causality by selective colonization.
- **SPF (specific-pathogen-free)** — standard lab mouse; has microbiome but lacks defined pathogens.
- **'Humanized' mice**: germ-free mice colonized with human microbiome — used for mechanistic + therapeutic studies. Gordon lab pioneered.

**FMT — fecal microbiota transplantation**:
- Donor stool processed + administered via colonoscopy, retention enema, nasoduodenal tube, or oral capsules.
- Highly effective (~85-90%) for **recurrent C. difficile**.
- Investigated for IBD (mixed), metabolic syndrome (mixed), autism, depression, GVHD, infection prevention in ICU.
- Modern + better-controlled approaches: defined microbial consortia (Vedanta, Seres, Vowst — purified *Firmicutes* spores), engineered probiotics.
- Risks: rare donor-derived ESBL-producing *E. coli* transmission (FDA 2019 warning, two deaths in immunocompromised); careful screening essential.

slides.title: Metagenomics, single-cell + long-read genomics for microbiology
slides.body:
The biggest revolution in modern microbiology is **culture-independent**, **community-scale**, **multi-omic** sequencing. Most microbes (>99%) remain uncultured — but we can read their genomes from the environment directly.

**16S rRNA gene surveys** — the foundational approach (**Norman Pace** + Stahl + Olsen 1985+):
- PCR-amplify variable regions (V3-V4, V4, V1-V2) of the 16S rRNA gene from total community DNA → sequence (Illumina MiSeq workhorse).
- Cluster sequences into **OTUs (operational taxonomic units)** at ~97% identity, or use **ASVs (amplicon sequence variants; Callahan + Holmes 2016 DADA2)** for exact-sequence-level resolution.
- Map to reference databases: **SILVA, Greengenes, RDP, GTDB**.
- Output: community composition + relative abundance per sample.
- **Limitations**: copy-number variation in 16S genes; PCR + primer biases; resolution to genus often (species sometimes); no functional information.

**Shotgun metagenomics** — sequence total community DNA without targeted PCR:
- Captures all genes — functional repertoire + taxonomy + strain-level resolution.
- **Assembly + binning**: assemble contigs from short reads → cluster contigs into **MAGs (metagenome-assembled genomes)** via tetranucleotide composition + coverage co-variation across samples. Tools: metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT, MetaBAT2, CONCOCT, MaxBin2, DAS_Tool, anvi'o.
- **Tyson + Banfield 2004** (*Nature*) — **acid mine drainage at Iron Mountain, California**: assembled near-complete genomes of *Leptospirillum*, *Ferroplasma* + archaea directly from environment — the **founding metagenomics paper**. Demonstrated that genome assembly from communities was feasible.
- ***Jill Banfield*** (Berkeley) lab continued + pushed metagenomics: discovered the **CPR (Candidate Phyla Radiation, 2015)** — 26% of bacterial diversity, mostly ultrasmall episymbionts, almost entirely uncultured. Massive expansion of the tree of life.
- Reference databases: **GTDB (Genome Taxonomy Database, Parks + Hugenholtz 2018+)** — standardized phylogenomic-based taxonomy across ~400000 genomes; reshuffled bacterial + archaeal nomenclature. **NCBI RefSeq, GenBank, Ensembl Bacteria**.
- **Functional annotation**: gene prediction (Prodigal); functional databases (KEGG, COG, Pfam, eggNOG, CAZy, MEROPS, ARG-databases like CARD).

**Single-cell genomics** — sequence one cell at a time:
- **scRNA-seq for microbes** — limited by tiny RNA content; emerging (PETRI-seq, BacDrop, MicroSPLiT — 10x Genomics partnership 2023).
- **Single-cell genomics (SAG)** — sort individual cells (FACS or microfluidic), MDA whole-genome amplification, sequence → genome per cell. Allows access to uncultured organisms one at a time. Stepanauskas + DeLong + Woyke pioneered.
- **Hi-C metagenomics** — chromosome conformation capture in communities; allows linking of plasmids/phages to their host (DovetailGenomics, PhaseGenomics).
- **proximity-tagging + scaffolding**.

**Long-read sequencing** — read length transforms metagenomics:
- **PacBio HiFi** — ~10-25 kb reads, >99% accuracy. Allows complete genome assembly from environmental samples + recovery of large mobile elements.
- **Oxford Nanopore** — reads up to Mb-scale; portable (MinION palm-sized used in field deployments — Ebola West Africa surveillance, SARS-CoV-2 ARTIC, antibiotic-resistance gene rapid profiling on R10.4 flow cells). Real-time sequencing — first results in minutes.
- Long reads resolve **structural variation**, **mobile elements**, **rRNA + repetitive operons**, **complete plasmids + phages**, **circular elements**, **assembly through repeats** — all things short reads struggle with.
- **Smith + Pevzner** — **Hamilton Smith** (Nobel 1978 for restriction enzymes; Venter Institute co-founder) + **Pavel Pevzner** (UCSD) developed key genome-assembly algorithms — de-Bruijn-graph assemblers (SPAdes lineage); enable modern metagenomics + single-cell assemblies.
- **Hybrid assemblies** — short + long reads combined; current best-practice for complete bacterial genomes.

**Metatranscriptomics, metaproteomics, metabolomics**:
- Read RNA, proteins, metabolites from the community → functional activity, not just gene presence.
- Tara Oceans + EMP increasingly multi-omic.

**Earth Microbiome Project (Knight + colleagues 2010-)**:
- Globally standardized sampling + 16S/metagenomic processing across all biomes (oceans, soils, host-associated, built environment, extreme environments). ~30000+ samples.
- Reveals biogeography + diversity drivers + previously unknown lineages. 
- **GTDB** + EMP-based taxonomy reshapes the tree of life with hundreds of new phyla.

**Banfield CPR (Candidate Phyla Radiation)** discovery (Brown, Castelle + Banfield 2015 *Nature*):
- Reconstruction of >1000 nearly complete bacterial genomes from groundwater + sediment metagenomes.
- Identified ~70+ candidate phyla in a single radiation — **CPR** — encompassing Saccharibacteria (TM7), Parcubacteria, Microgenomates, others.
- Ultrasmall (~0.2-0.3 μm), reduced biosynthetic capacity → likely episymbionts on other bacteria.
- **DPANN archaea** — analogous reduced-genome radiation among archaea.
- Together they dramatically expanded the tree of life + revealed that most microbial diversity is uncultivated.

Modern microbiology runs on culture-independent sequencing. The historical 'great plate-count anomaly' (>99% of microbes uncultured) is becoming the 'great metagenomic feast' (most microbial genomes accessible via sequencing) — though cultivation + experimental tractability remain rate-limiting for mechanistic biology.

slides.title: AI + synthetic biology + the future of microbiology
slides.body:
Microbiology is now a **computational + AI-augmented** discipline. The convergence of metagenomics, structural biology, protein design + ML is reshaping discovery, diagnostics + therapy.

**AlphaFold + structural biology for microbiology**:
- **AlphaFold** (Jumper et al. 2021; Hassabis + Jumper + Baker Nobel Chemistry 2024) predicts structures from sequence (covered in structural-biology lesson). **AFDB** has >200M structures including virtually every protein from every sequenced microbe.
- **Applications**:
  - **Antibody structure prediction** for vaccine + therapeutic design (AlphaFold-Multimer + RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN); HIV bNAb design; SARS-CoV-2 spike-antibody complexes; *Plasmodium* antigen design.
  - **Microbial functional annotation** — for proteins with no detectable sequence homologs, AF-predicted structure + Foldseek + DALI find structural homologs → infer function.
  - **Antibiotic target structure** — KPC carbapenemase, NDM-1, MCR-1, AcrB efflux, ribosomal mutants — all accessible.
  - **Vaccine antigen design** — stabilized prefusion antigens (RSV F, SARS-CoV-2 S, HIV Env trimer, malaria PfRH5) using AF + RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN.
  - **De novo binders** to microbial targets (Baker lab miniproteins binding SARS-CoV-2 spike, influenza HA, others).
  - **Microbial toxin structures** + neutralizing antibody design.

**AMR prediction + AI antibiotic discovery**:
- ***Jonathan Stokes + James Collins*** (MIT + McMaster) 2020 *Cell*: deep neural networks trained on ~2500 known antibiotic + non-antibiotic molecules screened libraries of millions; identified **halicin** — a previously known c-Met inhibitor — as a broad-spectrum antibiotic with activity against *Acinetobacter*, *M. tuberculosis*, *C. difficile*. **Demonstrated ML-driven antibiotic discovery as a viable paradigm**.
- **Subsequent work** — Stokes + Collins + others: **abaucin** (selective anti-*Acinetobacter baumannii* compound, Liu + Stokes 2023); discovery of antibiotics from soil + human + animal microbiomes via ML virtual screening; generative chemistry models (de novo molecule design).
- **AMR-gene prediction from genomes**: ML models (NCBI AMRFinderPlus, CARD-RGI, ResFinder, hAMRonization frameworks) identify resistance genes from sequences; ML extending to predict resistance phenotypes from genotype + environment (Galagan + Collins TB resistance prediction; Yeats + Pacheco AMR forecasting).
- **Rapid diagnostic ML**: Nanopore + ML for real-time pathogen + AMR identification at point of care.

**LLM-augmented genomics + biology**:
- **Protein language models**: ESM-2 + ESM-3 (Meta — Rives, Lin + colleagues), ProtBERT, ProGen, RoseTTAFoldNA, AbLang, Boltz-1/2, Chai-1, AlphaFold 3. Encode 'biology of proteins' as deep representations; useful for predicting function, fitness, interactions, design. Microbial proteomes (which dominate sequence-space diversity) anchor training.
- **Genomic language models**: Nucleotide Transformer, DNABERT, HyenaDNA, Evo (Hie + colleagues 2024). Predict regulatory + coding consequences of sequence changes.
- **Biology-aware LLMs**: BioGPT, Med-PaLM 2, OpenBioML, Galactica successors — augment scientific literature mining, microbial-pathogen identification, diagnostic suggestion.
- **Microbial proteome + secondary-metabolite mining**: AI-augmented BGC (biosynthetic gene cluster) discovery — antiSMASH, BiG-SCAPE + ML extensions; identifies new natural-product candidates (Medema lab + others).
- **Generative chemistry + protein design**: combine RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + ESM + AF3 → design de novo enzymes + binders + sensors against microbial targets.

**Synthetic biology + engineered microbes**:
- ***Chris Voigt*** (MIT) — pioneer of bacterial genetic circuits, microbial-foundry approaches, large-scale circuit design + automated DNA construction. Genetic circuit-design tools (Cello, COMET).
- ***Drew Endy*** (Stanford + iGEM founder) — co-founder of synthetic biology; iGEM (international Genetically Engineered Machines competition since 2003) trained a generation of synthetic biologists worldwide.
- ***Tom Knight, Ron Weiss, James Collins, Tim Lu, Pamela Silver*** + others built the modern synthetic-biology toolkit.
- **Engineered probiotics + live biotherapeutics**: engineered *E. coli Nissle*, *Lactococcus*, *Bacteroides*, *Akkermansia* for: PKU (Synlogic SYNB1618 + SYNB1934), bile-acid disorders, immune modulation (anti-PD-1 enhancement), cancer (engineered *Salmonella*, *Listeria* — historical Coley toxins + modern descendants), microbiome modulation.
- **Metabolic engineering** — engineered yeasts + bacteria for: insulin + recombinant proteins (the original biotech industry); artemisinic acid (Keasling — Amyris/Sanofi semi-synthetic artemisinin); cannabinoids; opiates (Smolke lab); morphinan + tropane alkaloids; food (Impossible Foods leghemoglobin via *Pichia* yeast; Perfect Day milk proteins via *Trichoderma*); biofuels (Joule, LS9 — historical; Solazyme/TerraVia).
- **Cell-free systems** — synthetic-biology subset (Jewett + Noireaux + Voigt + Murray); microbial extracts producing proteins on-demand. Diagnostics (SHERLOCK Cas13 — Collins/Zhang/Daringer), vaccines, education.
- **JCVI Synthia + Mycoplasma minimal genomes (Venter, Hutchison, Smith 2010-2016)**: chemically synthesized + booted up the entire genome of *Mycoplasma mycoides* → *Synthia* / *Mycoplasma laboratorium*. Then JCVI-syn3.0 (473 genes — minimal genome of any free-living cell). Roadmap toward designed life.
- **DNA synthesis + assembly** — Gibson Assembly (Daniel Gibson 2009), Golden Gate (Engler), MoClo + Yeast Toolkit, Twist Bioscience + IDT + Ansa synthesis services; cost has dropped ~1000× in 15 years.
- **CRISPR-based microbial engineering**: Cas9 + Cas12 + CRISPRi/a (Gilbert + Qi + Weissman) for any tractable bacterium; expanded genetic tools for previously non-model microbes (Bacteroides, Akkermansia, *Clostridia*, Mycobacterium, Cyanobacteria, marine isolates).

**Other modern frontiers**:
- **Phage therapy + lysins** — covered in virology lesson; AI + structure-guided phage engineering.
- **mRNA vaccines for bacterial + parasitic diseases** (BioNTech malaria, TB, S. aureus pipelines).
- **Microbial diagnostics**: metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for unbiased pathogen detection (Chiu, Wilson UCSF — clinical mNGS for meningoencephalitis + sepsis); rapid sequencing-based ID (Nanopore at-bedside).
- ***Microbial dark matter*** characterization continues: thousands of candidate phyla still to be cultured + characterized.
- **One Health + climate**: linking human, animal + environmental microbiomes; zoonotic surveillance; permafrost-microbe climate feedbacks; antibiotic-resistance gene spread across human-animal-environment interfaces.
- **Astrobiology** + Mars + Europa / Enceladus / Titan microbial-life targets — biosignatures from earth extremophiles inform mission design.

The field is now multidisciplinary in a deeper sense than ever: microbiologists work alongside AI researchers, structural biologists, synthetic chemists, biophysicists, ecologists, clinicians, regulators + entrepreneurs. The trajectory from van Leeuwenhoek's lens to AlphaFold-designed antibody therapies + iGEM-trained synthetic biologists is one of the great arcs of modern science.

question.question: Design a clinical microbiome study + intervention
question.goal: Plan a study to evaluate microbiome modulation for recurrent C. difficile, integrating modern tools (metagenomics, FMT alternatives, mechanistic readouts).

acceptedAnswers: Defined microbial consortium restores colonization resistance + prevents recurrence; primary endpoint = recurrence-free at 8 weeks

steps.reveal: **Hypothesis**: a defined microbial consortium (vs traditional FMT) restores colonization resistance against C. difficile via bile-acid + SCFA + niche competition. **Primary endpoint**: recurrence-free survival at 8 weeks post-treatment (analogous to PUNCH-CD3/Rebyota + ECOSPOR-III/Vowst trials). Secondary endpoints: time-to-recurrence, microbiome restoration metrics, quality of life, safety.

acceptedAnswers: Randomized placebo-controlled trial; ~200-300 patients per arm; stratify by # of prior C. diff episodes

steps.reveal: **Design**: multicenter RCT, stratified by prior C. diff episodes (≥2 vs ≥3), with placebo (or standard-of-care vancomycin + bezlotoxumab) control. ~250 patients per arm to detect ~20% absolute reduction in recurrence (assuming ~35% control recurrence rate, 80% power). Adaptive designs + Bayesian methods increasingly used.

acceptedAnswers: Shotgun metagenomics + metabolomics + bile-acid panels + immune profiling + strain-tracking

steps.reveal: **Multi-omic monitoring**: shotgun metagenomics (Illumina + Nanopore for plasmid/strain tracking; Smith-Pevzner-style assembly); metabolomics (bile acids — secondary bile acid producers Clostridium scindens key for colonization resistance); SCFAs; immune profiling (Treg, IgA, AMPs); strain-tracking via SNP-level analysis (StrainPhlAn, inStrain). Use **GTDB-based taxonomy** (Knight + Hugenholtz). Single-cell genomics (Banfield/Woyke style) for uncultured members.

acceptedAnswers: Defined consortia (Rebyota, Vowst), engineered probiotics (Synlogic), phage-based depletion of C. diff, ML-designed cocktails

steps.reveal: Modern options: (1) **defined microbial consortia** — Seres/Vowst (Firmicutes spores, oral); Rebyota (broad consortium, rectal); Vedanta VE303 (8-strain Clostridia); (2) **engineered probiotics** (Synlogic *E. coli Nissle* for metabolic disease; could be adapted); (3) **phage-based C. diff depletion** (Locus + others); (4) **ML-designed personalized consortia** based on patient microbiome profile + colonization-resistance scoring; (5) **anti-C. diff antibodies** (bezlotoxumab already approved). Aim: cleaner safety profile + reproducibility than donor stool.

acceptedAnswers: Live Biotherapeutic Product (LBP) FDA category; GMP production; donor + product safety screening; CMC

steps.reveal: FDA **Live Biotherapeutic Product (LBP)** regulatory category (CBER); GMP manufacturing for defined consortia + spore preparations; donor (for traditional FMT) extensive screening (ESBL *E. coli* deaths in 2019 led to enhanced screening). Cold chain, viable-organism release assays, batch-to-batch reproducibility — major manufacturing challenges. Two FDA-approved LBPs as of 2024 (Rebyota Nov 2022; Vowst Apr 2023) opened the path.

question.question: Why is the Banfield + Tyson 2004 Iron Mountain acid-mine-drainage metagenomics paper considered a landmark?
options: **Tyson + Banfield 2004** (*Nature*) was the first paper to **assemble near-complete genomes of multiple microbial species directly from an environmental sample**, without cultivation. They sequenced biofilm DNA from acid mine drainage at Iron Mountain (CA; pH ~0.5; 40 °C) → assembled essentially complete genomes of *Leptospirillum* group II + III + partial *Ferroplasma* + Archaea. **Founded metagenomic genome assembly** as a discipline + demonstrated that the >99% uncultured microbial majority becomes accessible via sequencing. Subsequent work by **Banfield + colleagues** (CPR/Candidate Phyla Radiation 2015, ~70 new candidate phyla; DPANN archaea; thousands of MAGs) massively expanded the tree of life + revealed that **most microbial diversity is uncultured**. Foundation of modern metagenomics — combined with **Smith + Pevzner**-class assembly algorithms (de-Bruijn graphs, SPAdes) + GTDB taxonomy (Parks + Hugenholtz) + Earth Microbiome Project (Knight) — created the modern computational microbial ecology field.
question.explanation: Tyson + Banfield (2004 Nature) — Iron Mountain acid-mine-drainage biofilm metagenomics — first paper to assemble near-complete genomes of multiple species directly from environment without cultivation. Founded metagenomic genome assembly as a discipline. Banfield lab subsequently discovered CPR (~70 candidate phyla, 2015) + thousands of MAGs. Foundation of modern culture-independent microbiology + tree-of-life expansion.

slides.workedSolution: Tyson + Banfield (2004 Nature) assembled near-complete genomes of Leptospirillum + Ferroplasma directly from Iron Mountain acid-mine drainage biofilm — without cultivation. First metagenomic genome assembly. Founded modern metagenomics + Banfield's CPR discoveries (2015). Combined with Smith-Pevzner assembly algorithms + GTDB + Earth Microbiome Project, created modern culture-independent microbial ecology.

question.question: End-to-end AI-driven antibiotic discovery
question.prompt: You are leading an AI-driven antibiotic discovery program targeting MDR *Acinetobacter baumannii*. Outline an end-to-end pipeline integrating: (1) target identification (essential-gene metagenomics + AlphaFold structures); (2) virtual screening — molecular docking + ML scoring (Stokes-Collins halicin paradigm; chemical-language models like Chemformer + Graph NNs); (3) generative chemistry for novel scaffolds (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN for protein binders, MolMIM + REINVENT for small molecules); (4) experimental validation pipeline (high-throughput screen + iChip-cultivated isolates after Lewis/teixobactin); (5) resistance + safety profiling. Reference Davies + O'Neill + Stokes + Collins + Lewis.

question.question: Roughly what fraction of human gut microbial cells were once estimated to outnumber human cells (older 'classic' ratio)? And what's the revised modern estimate?
question.hint: Sender, Fuchs + Milo 2016 PLoS Biology revision.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, summarize the modern + frontier landscape of microbiology.
question.rubric: Mentions: microbiome — HMP (NIH 2007-2014) characterized human microbiome at 18 sites; iHMP integrated disease cohorts; Earth Microbiome Project (Knight); Gordon germ-free + obesity + malnutrition. Disease links: obesity, IBD, IBS, C. diff (FMT 85-90% cure → FDA LBPs Rebyota + Vowst), immunotherapy response. Metagenomics: 16S Pace; shotgun + binning + MAGs (Tyson + Banfield 2004 Iron Mountain acid-mine drainage founding paper; Banfield CPR ~70 candidate phyla 2015; DPANN archaea; GTDB taxonomy). Single-cell genomics; Hi-C; long-read Oxford Nanopore + PacBio HiFi (portable field deployment); Smith + Pevzner assembly algorithms. AI for microbiology: AlphaFold + AFDB for microbial protein annotation + antibody + vaccine design; halicin (Stokes + Collins 2020 ML antibiotic discovery); abaucin; LLMs + protein language models (ESM); generative chemistry. Synthetic biology — Voigt circuits + Endy iGEM + engineered probiotics (Synlogic) + Venter/JCVI minimal genome syn3.0 + Keasling artemisinic acid. AMR remains existential (O'Neill). Concludes: microbiology is now culture-independent, AI-augmented + cross-disciplinary; from van Leeuwenhoek's lens to designed live biotherapeutics + AlphaFold-guided antibody-engineered vaccines, the trajectory is one of the great arcs of modern science.
